title: Ledi-Geraru jaw, earliest known Homo, Ethiopia
summary: A partial lower jaw with five teeth from the Ledi-Geraru area of Ethiopia's Afar region was reported in 2015 as the earliest evidence of the genus Homo, dated 2.80 to 2.75 million years ago. It mixes primitive features of early Australopithecus with later Homo traits and is about 400,000 years older than previously known Homo fossils.

uncertainty.note: Years before present in the sources are written here as negative calendar years without subtracting 1950; the sources give rounded ages. The Science abstract states the range directly.
